title: Alphita headword-reference graph as an independently named reconstruction target
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: test whether independently delimited Voynich entries preserve a medieval glossary's directed headword-reference network under one unknown global name mapping. Alphita supplies a concrete external primary-text edition and explicit Respice references; no botanical image identifications are required.

design.mechanism: A glossary encodes each headword consistently and refers to other headwords inside its entries. A shared unknown injective headword map must preserve directed reference incidence across entries, including references not used to infer the map.
design.external_source: Mowat's 1887 edition of Alphita, Bodleian Selden B.35; University of Glasgow copy, BHL item 179915, DOI 10.5962/bhl.title.100685; https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/179915 ; readable OCR https://archive.org/stream/b21463955/b21463955_djvu.txt . The bound volume includes other works: isolate Alphita proper and separate edition apparatus, variant witness readings and editorial notes before extraction.
design.source_example: Alphita's Absinthium entry explicitly directs the reader to centonica and sandonicum. The printed edition marks witness omissions with brackets; the exact selected witness must therefore be frozen. These are directed reference targets, not permission to equate the three names.
design.target_representation: Prospective narrow hypothesis: one independently marked admitted Herbal paragraph is one entry; its first definite complete raw group is the headword. Every exact occurrence of another admitted entry headword within that paragraph is an observed directed mention. No inherited workshop POS, root stripping, inferred species or adaptive entry boundaries. No target query has been made for this proposal.
design.prediction: One mapping inferred from a frozen subset must predict which particular headword strings occur as targets in held entries. Source Respice edges are required mention edges, not an exhaustive inventory of all source mentions: extra target mentions cannot automatically be called errors. For a closed-world comparison use separately extracted complete source headword-mention incidence, with all omissions explicit.
design.falsifier: No single injective global mapping realizes the required source edges within the fixed target entry frame, or all surviving mappings disagree on every held reference. A positive result requires specific shared held predictions and an explicit account of alternative mappings, including graph automorphisms; degree similarity alone is insufficient.
design.smallest_test: Within two hours isolate and manually check one fixed contiguous Alphita headword block plus its referenced headwords; compute its ambiguity and a prospective held-edge prediction before any target scoring. Then preregister exact admitted paragraph selectors and entry boundaries. Stop if the source fragment has no informative network or target entry ownership cannot be independently defined; do not replace this with a generic decoder benchmark.
design.nearest_predecessors: GDT214/GDT187 concern hydraulic label-to-same-page-prose reuse, not a source-named directed glossary graph. GDT341/342 concern record-local anonymous recipe event/flow graphs, not global persistent headwords. Registry search Alphita returned zero; this is bounded novelty screening, not proof that the historical source was never encountered.
design.scope_note: RAW_UNSCREENED and unreviewed. The text being a glossary, first-group headwords, fixed name encoding and source relationship are hypotheses. No Voynich query, image, graph score or source relationship is established by intake. Preserve f84/f84r sealing and source-entry scope gates. This proposal does not reopen existing scored label-prose panels automatically.
